description: A cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a large ribosomal subunit; includes transport to the sites of protein synthesis. [GOC:jl]
label: RIBOSOMAL LARGE SUBUNIT BIOGENESIS *

description: A cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of ribosome subunits; includes transport to the sites of protein synthesis. [GOC:ma, PMID:26404467, Wikipedia:Ribosome_biogenesis]
label: RIBOSOME BIOGENESIS *

description: The directed, self-propelled movement of a cilium. [GOC:dph, GOC:jl]
label: CILIUM MOVEMENT *

description: Any process involved in the conversion of a primary ribosomal RNA (rRNA) transcript into one or more mature rRNA molecules. [GOC:curators]
label: RRNA PROCESSING *

description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving rRNA, ribosomal RNA, a structural constituent of ribosomes. [ISBN:0198506732]
label: RRNA METABOLIC PROCESS *

description: A cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a small ribosomal subunit; includes transport to the sites of protein synthesis. [GOC:jl]
label: RIBOSOMAL SMALL SUBUNIT BIOGENESIS *

label: CILIUM OR FLAGELLUM DEPENDENT CELL MOTILITY *

description: A cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a complex containing RNA and proteins. [GOC:isa_complete, GOC:mah]
label: RIBONUCLEOPROTEIN COMPLEX BIOGENESIS *

description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lipid stimulus. [GOC:sl]
label: RESPONSE TO LIPID *

description: A cellular process involving delivery of a portion of the cytoplasm to lysosomes or to the plant or fungal vacuole that does not involve direct transport through the endocytic or vacuolar protein sorting (Vps) pathways. This process typically leads to degradation of the cargo; however, it can also be used to deliver resident proteins, such as in the cytoplasm-to-vacuole targeting (Cvt) pathway. [PMID:21997368, PMID:22966490, PMID:28596378]
label: PROCESS UTILIZING AUTOPHAGIC MECHANISM *

description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of substances. [GOC:go_curators]
label: POSITIVE REGULATION OF CATABOLIC PROCESS *

description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nitrogen compound stimulus. [GOC:pr, GOC:TermGenie]
label: CELLULAR RESPONSE TO NITROGEN COMPOUND *

description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stress acting at the endoplasmic reticulum. ER stress usually results from the accumulation of unfolded or misfolded proteins in the ER lumen. [GOC:cjm, GOC:mah]
label: RESPONSE TO ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM STRESS *

description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipids, compounds soluble in an organic solvent but not, or sparingly, in an aqueous solvent. [GOC:go_curators]
label: LIPID BIOSYNTHETIC PROCESS *

description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a peptide hormone stimulus. A peptide hormone is any of a class of peptides that are secreted into the blood stream and have endocrine functions in living animals. [GOC:mah]
label: CELLULAR RESPONSE TO PEPTIDE HORMONE STIMULUS *

description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of a multi-organism process in which a virus is a participant. [GOC:bf, GOC:jl]
label: NEGATIVE REGULATION OF VIRAL PROCESS *
